speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history. To better understand your gait and limb ataxia, can you describe when these symptoms first appeared and if they have been progressive?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: These symptoms are concerning for a cerebellar lesion. Have you experienced any double vision, slurred speech, or weakness in your limbs as well? Also, do you have any history of head trauma or recent infections?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast focusing on the cerebellum and brainstem.
REQUEST TEST: Cerebrospinal Fluid (CSF) analysis for JC virus PCR.
Given your history of Crohn's disease and natalizumab use, this presentation raises a high suspicion for Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML).

OBSERVATION_ATTACK.clean_observation: RESULTS: MRI Brain: Lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML). T1/T2 images showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of PML. CSF Analysis: JC Virus PCR positive.
